BUILD_PROMPT.SYSTEM_ROLE: Senior full-stack engineer turning the existing localhost Task Dashboard (omes-bot, omega_prime.dashboard, PR #47) into the "Omega Prime Command Center": a polished, animated, read-only operator console. Planned by Sol, built by Luna, run inside /workspace/omp-sandbox (OpenShell on rootless Podman, Anda-signed access).
BUILD_PROMPT.APP_CONTEXT: The dashboard today is a Python server (omega_prime.dashboard) bound to 127.0.0.1:7421 with collectors for Herdr panes, omp processes, wiring-phase runs, sandbox e2e, omega jobs, podman, GitHub PRs and Greptile scores, plus tasks.json at ~/.omega-prime/dashboard. It serves static HTML/JS with SSE plus polling, strict redaction, security headers and Host checks, on branch feat/task-dashboard (PR #47, not merged). The 21st.dev MCP is already connected (user-21st) and should be used to find and pull components, themes and logos.

SCOPE.SHELL_LAYOUT: A real dashboard shell. On the left, a sidebar with a numbered task list (filter and search, state badges, selection). In the main pane, the selected task's detail. Top-level views: Overview, Tasks, CI/CD, Repositories, plus room for more views later.
SCOPE.TASK_NUMBERING: Every task gets a stable sequential id formatted "00001 - TITLE": five digits zero-padded, a space, a hyphen, a space, then the title. The id is assigned once, persisted in tasks.json, never reused, and shown identically in the sidebar, the detail view, chat and future Task Board rows. Existing tasks are back-filled in their current order starting at 00001.
SCOPE.CI_CD_VIEW: Per-PR and per-branch CI checks across the org's open PRs: check names, conclusions, durations, failing jobs with a link-out, Greptile score with its reviewed commit, and merge-order state for the wiring phases.
SCOPE.REPOSITORIES_VIEW: An overview of the swcstudiospace GitHub org's repositories: name, visibility, default branch, last push, open PR count, latest main CI status and language. Sortable and searchable, with links to GitHub.
SCOPE.OVERVIEW_VIEW: Command-center summary: counts of active, waiting-on-Ove, PR-gate and finished items, recent merges, source health, and a live activity feed.
SCOPE.TASK_DETAIL: Owner, source, state, model, started and last-activity times in AEDT, progress, links (PR, logs, Herdr pane), and a timeline of state changes.

DESIGN_SYSTEM_CONTINUITY.COLOUR: Omega Prime white and purple: a white/near-white base, purple primary accent and gradients, with neutral greys for text. Contrast at least WCAG AA. An optional dark variant is allowed but light is the default.
DESIGN_SYSTEM_CONTINUITY.TYPOGRAPHY: Use the typeface used on Greptile's marketing website (greptile.com). Identify it by inspecting the live site's CSS rather than guessing. Self-host it only if its licence allows. Otherwise use the closest freely licensed match, and record the decision.
DESIGN_SYSTEM_CONTINUITY.MOTION: Animations from Magic UI and Aceternity UI components, found via the 21st.dev MCP or their official registries: subtle card entrances, number tickers for counts, a border or beam effect on active items, and a shimmer for loading. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Never block data display on an animation.

BUILD_PROMPT.PLATFORM_CONSTRAINTS: Magic UI and Aceternity are React, Tailwind and framer-motion libraries, so the front end becomes a small React app built to static assets. The existing Python server keeps serving it plus the JSON/SSE API. No Node server at runtime. The build happens inside the sandbox, and the built assets are committed or packaged so the Python package serves them.
BUILD_PROMPT.SECURITY_AND_VALIDATION: Keep everything PR #47 guarantees: bind only to loopback (refuse 0.0.0.0 and ::), read-only (non-GET returns 405), Host header check, CSP and security headers, redaction of secrets in every payload, no innerHTML with untrusted data, and the GitHub token via the credential broker or env and never sent to the browser. CSP must allow only self-hosted fonts and scripts, with no third-party CDNs at runtime. The org repo listing is read-only.
BUILD_PROMPT.STATES: Each view has loading (shimmer), empty, error (source down, with a retry), stale (last updated more than N seconds ago) and partial states. GitHub rate-limit and offline states degrade gracefully while the local sections keep working.
BUILD_PROMPT.GRACEFUL_DEGRADATION: If GitHub is unreachable, the CI/CD and Repositories views show cached data with an age badge. If SSE fails, it falls back to polling. If JS fails, the existing minimal page or a clear message shows.
BUILD_PROMPT.WORKFLOW: Run in /workspace/omp-sandbox on the openshell-podman tier. Sol plans (GSD plan phase) and Luna executes, on the ChatGPT plan with thinking on auto and no time caps. The worktree is mounted into the sandbox. Commits stay local until exported, then are pushed from the host as a new branch stacked on feat/task-dashboard, with a draft PR and the Greptile loop. Never merge.
BUILD_PROMPT.CONSTRAINTS: Do not invent repository facts, file paths, package versions or API routes. Discover them. No system-wide installs; Node and pnpm or npm stay user-local or inside the sandbox image. No deploys or Railway or VPS changes. Never print tokens or argv. Keep the dashboard running on 7421 until the new build is verified, then restart it on the new head.

NODE.QUESTION: Which file-disjoint units make up the Command Center?

RATIONALE.STEP: Task numbering unit: a seq/num field and next_seq counter in tasks.json, back-fill in current order from 00001, never reuse, plus a CLI helper and a read-only API field for display_id.

API unit: extend the github collector to the org (repos list, open PRs for omes-bot and coding-fleet, check runs per head SHA, Greptile score with reviewed commit), cached with an age badge and rate-limit handling.

Frontend shell unit: a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind app under omega_prime/dashboard/frontend, built to omega_prime/dashboard/static/cc with hashed assets, served by the existing Python server.
Views unit: Overview, Tasks (sidebar list plus detail with timeline), CI/CD, Repositories, each with loading, empty, error, stale and partial states.
Design unit: white and purple tokens, self-hosted Greptile typefaces, Magic UI and Aceternity components adapted as local sources with reduced-motion handling.
Pipeline unit: sandbox seed, npm install and build, pytest and the frontend tests inside the sandbox, then export commits to the host.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Six units: numbering, API, shell, views, design, pipeline. Numbering and API are Python-only; shell, views and design are frontend-only; the pipeline touches only omp-sandbox and a build script.

NODE.QUESTION: Which typeface, tokens and animation components does the Command Center use?

RATIONALE.STEP: Inspect greptile.com's live CSS: @font-face rules declare Anybody (h1 and body default), Space Mono (most UI copy, .font-mono) and DM Sans (.font-sans), loaded through next/font.
All three are Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, so self-host them from the @fontsource packages (woff2 plus licence files) bundled by Vite.
Define tokens: white and near-white surfaces, purple primary (violet 600/700 family) with gradients, neutral grey text, all checked for WCAG AA contrast.
Pick Magic UI (MIT): Number Ticker, Blur Fade, Border Beam and Animated Shiny Text (shimmer) via 21st.dev ids 1282 and 1079 plus the magicui.design registry.
Pick Aceternity: Sidebar (animated, expandable) and Card Hover Effect from the ui.aceternity.com registry; skip Card Spotlight because it pulls three.js.
Wrap every animation in a prefers-reduced-motion check (motion's useReducedMotion plus a CSS media query) and never gate data on animation completion.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Fonts: Anybody (display), Space Mono (UI/mono), DM Sans (body), OFL, self-hosted. Components: Magic UI Number Ticker, Blur Fade, Border Beam, Animated Shiny Text; Aceternity Sidebar, Card Hover Effect.

NODE.QUESTION: How is a React UI built and shipped inside a Python package with a self-only CSP?

RATIONALE.STEP: Option A, React + Vite static build committed to the package: no Node at runtime, hashed JS and CSS, fonts as local assets; fits script-src 'self'.
Option B, Preact or vanilla with hand-ported animations: smaller, but loses Magic UI and Aceternity fidelity, which the ask names explicitly.
Option C, a runtime Node server: rejected by the platform constraint.

CSP check: Vite output needs no inline scripts; motion uses inline style attributes, so style-src needs 'self' plus 'unsafe-inline' for style only, or the CSP keeps style-src 'self' if only CSS classes are used; scripts stay 'self'.
Packaging: built files under omega_prime/dashboard/static/cc, served by the existing static handler; the legacy page stays at /legacy as the no-JS fallback.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Option A. Commit the built assets; the CSP stays default-src 'self' with no external origins; style-src may need 'unsafe-inline' for motion's style attributes, documented.

NODE.QUESTION: What could break PR #47's guarantees or create licence and cost problems?

RATIONALE.STEP: Licence: the fonts are OFL (fine to self-host with OFL.txt); Magic UI is MIT; the Aceternity licence allows use in end products but forbids redistributing its source files, so adapt the components into the app with attribution and keep no verbatim registry dump in the repo.
Redaction: every new field (repo names, check names, job URLs, PR titles, task notes) must go through redact_value before it reaches the snapshot.
Rate limits: org repo listing and check runs are N+1 calls; cache for 60-120 s, cap pages, and degrade to cached data with an age badge on 403 or 429.
Bundle size and animation cost: keep the bundle under about 400 KB gzip, lazy-free; animations use transform and opacity only and stop under reduced motion.
Sandbox risk: Python tests need pytest staged from the host; the build writes only inside the sandbox workdir and commits leave only via the export path.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Risks are manageable with redaction, caching and the Aceternity adaptation rule. Open questions: none (defaults recorded as non-blocking clarifications).

NODE.QUESTION: In what order do Sol and Luna build it, and how is it verified and shipped?

RATIONALE.STEP: W1 (Python): task numbering in status_file.py and a new omega_prime/dashboard/task_ids.py plus CLI `python -m omega_prime.dashboard next-id`, with tests.
W2 (Python): github collector extension (org repos, PR checks, Greptile commit) and model/app API fields, with redaction and rate-limit tests.
W3 (frontend): Vite/React/Tailwind app in omega_prime/dashboard/frontend with the shell, four views, design tokens, fonts and components; build output committed to static/cc.
W4 (server): serve /cc assets as the default page, keep /legacy, tighten the CSP, and keep all PR #47 security tests green.
W5 (verify): pytest for the dashboard, frontend unit tests and build inside the sandbox; export commits; the host pushes feat/command-center and opens a draft PR stacked on #47.
W6 (ship): Greptile loop up to 5 rounds, restart the dashboard on 7421 from the verified head, and capture four screenshots.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Sol runs /gsd-plan-phase in the sandbox and writes the phase plans; Luna runs /gsd-execute-phase W1-W4 with atomic commits; the host does W5 export/push and W6. Never merge.

Components: Magic UI (MIT) Number Ticker, Blur Fade (21st.dev ids 1282, 1079), Border Beam, Animated Shiny Text (magicui.design registry); Aceternity Sidebar and Card Hover Effect (ui.aceternity.com registry), adapted into the app as end-product code with attribution. 21st.dev free code quota (2/day) was exhausted after two retrievals, so the rest came from the official registries.
